A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SMAAT and its intrinsic-dimensionality explanation of adversarial training, despite the changed title. All 16 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, safety-filter, retrieval, intrinsic-dimensionality, and layer-ablation experiments, including additional GLUE/AdvGLUE results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds decoder and vision layerwise training experiments, including GCG and PAIR evaluations.

M1.justification: SMAAT retains its twoNN-based layer selection, intermediate-layer PGD objective, and training of downstream layers while earlier layers are frozen. The new Algorithm 1 documents implementation; the targeted LAT experiments do not establish a change to SMAAT itself.

E1.justification: v2 adds generative-model training and evaluation using the LAT dataset, UltraChat, MT-Bench, and HarmBench GCG/PAIR attacks. This substantially extends coverage beyond v1's decoder dimensionality analysis, decoder classification experiment, and encoder-based safety filters. Existing classification, retrieval, and GLUE coverage remains.

E2.justification: DNE is removed from the detailed classification and runtime comparisons in Tables 1-2 and from baseline descriptions. It remains in the overview Figure 2, so its removal is incomplete. The other main comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include targeted residual-stream LAT at every even-numbered LLaMA layer, L2 bounds of 1-5, interleaved supervised fine-tuning, and MT-Bench/GCG/PAIR evaluation. VGG experiments sweep ReLU layers, attack strengths, and learning rates over 20 epochs. These are new evaluation designs; retained benchmark tables do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the investigation of how training layer affects robustness and generalization through LLaMA, BERT, and VGG configuration sweeps and an additional PAIR analysis (Figures 5-6). v1's separate first-versus-last-layer comparison across four models, in Appendix E/Figure 5, is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report runtime means and standard deviations over ten runs in Table 2. v2 adds no seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 1 averages training configurations but does not report new repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New layerwise results include GCG robustness reaching approximately 30% and PAIR robustness remaining above 75% across decoder configurations (Figure 6). Retained entries in Tables 1-5 are unchanged, while DNE table entries and the old endpoint-ablation results disappear. The overview also changes FreeLB++'s safety-filter point without a corresponding Table 3 update.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects layer-composition order and the projection-error indexing; Section 4 adds explicit smooth, compact manifold assumptions. v2 also introduces a twoNN inversion equation, printed without the minus sign required by its stated Pareto model. The main optimization objectives and complexity analysis remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The principal SMAAT and architecture-dependent ID claims remain. v2 extends its explanatory claim to multilayer decoder LAT and claims text-generation validation. Its abstract and conclusion also change the efficiency claim from using 25-33% of GPU time to reducing time by 25-33%, contradicting the retained introduction and runtime evidence.

C2.justification: v2 adds a tangent-space explanation for off-manifold perturbations and interprets decoder layer tradeoffs as explaining the benefit of multilayer LAT. The basic ID-to-robustness interpretation remains. v1's qualification about hunchback-shaped vision ID disappears, and some new descriptions reverse the ID directions shown in Figure 4.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reported public implementation link, SMAAT pseudocode covering perturbation initialization, cached representations and parameter updates, and decoder LAT implementation settings. It also newly identifies a 32-GB V100 GPU and 64 CPUs. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 integrates Casper and Sheshadri's latent adversarial training work into its motivation, explanatory contribution, and experiments. It adds a dedicated discussion of encoder/decoder attacks and references supporting the new generative evaluation. This substantially expands positioning around decoder LAT and jailbreak robustness beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, notation, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The former Approach section becomes separate layerwise-analysis and SMAAT sections, experimental discussion is reorganized, and appendices are remapped. Acknowledgement and impact sections are added.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text to a two-column layout, redraws the overview figures, reverses the ID/reconstruction-error plot rows, and introduces new decoder and multimodel scatterplots. The original endpoint bar chart is removed, an algorithm display is added, and comparison tables lose DNE rows or columns.

improvement.justification: The new decoder and vision layer sweeps provide more direct tests of the paper's explanatory hypothesis, while pseudocode, hardware details, and a code pointer improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removed DNE comparisons and newly inconsistent runtime claims, ID descriptions, and mathematical reporting. The net improvement is useful but limited.
